scope: All 43 figure-5.1 mnemonic families; page-wide OCR leads are not reviewed evidence.
evidence_policy: Documented, derived, consistency-supported extrapolation, hypothesis and unknown remain distinct. Printed source and chosen correction are both retained.

repertory.title: Figure 5.1: instruction repertory
repertory.comment: Primary baseline for all 43 mnemonic families, encodings, cycles and flag columns. Normalized zero glyphs and mnemonic spacing only; image remains authoritative.

formats.title: Instruction formats a–f
formats.comment: Explains flag encoding, SSX register selector, immediate bytes, address bytes and test/page selector fields.

load_intro.title: Figure 3.2: meaning of LRS
load_intro.comment: Introduces the CMC8 load operation; surrounding LDA/MOV examples belong to other architectures.

load_phases.title: LRS format and three phases
load_phases.comment: Fetch, operand-address fetch, final read; PC advances for both bytes. Also identifies REL as one cycle and JMP as two.

mops.title: Figure 4.2: MOP list
mops.comment: Numbered functional controls; not necessarily independent physical silicon wires.

datapath.title: Figure 4.1: processor principle diagram
datapath.comment: Register selectors, buses, ALU, latch paths and interrupt controls; explicitly simplified.

registers.title: Register addressing and X
registers.comment: PC=R(N), operand register=R(A); MOP20 selects R7/X; subroutines change N.

pages.title: Figure 4.3: page addressing
pages.comment: Four pages each for program/storage, AB-only I/O; LSX retains three cycles to simplify control.

lrs_timing.title: Figure 4.9: LRS bus timing
lrs_timing.comment: Memory enables, address changes and data-valid deadlines.

lrs_format.title: LRS encoding and read deadlines
lrs_format.comment: 01010RRR plus address byte; F1/F2 read timing and 375 ns example.

fetch.title: Common fetch description
fetch.comment: Common through T5; one-cycle instructions use T6/T7. IR open during T5.

fetch_mops.title: Figure 4.10: fetch controls
fetch_mops.comment: Numbered fetch table and alternatives; MOP6 needed by stores at F1T6.

lrs_function.title: Figure 4.11: LRS functional microprogram
lrs_function.comment: All three phases; IR final capture at end T5, BR capture at start T5.

lrs_mops.title: Figure 4.12 and SRS differences
lrs_mops.comment: Full LRS MOP table with recorded MOP1/2 errors; section 3.4 explains store signaling changes.

srs_timing.title: Figure 4.13: SRS timing
srs_timing.comment: Store output direction, early SME and WRITE pulse; contains no full numbered SRS table.

ein_text.title: Interrupt enable delay
ein_text.comment: EIN sets INTE at next instruction F0T2; request gating and interrupt entry overview.

interrupt_return.title: Figure 4.18: interrupt state flow
interrupt_return.comment: N increments on interrupt entry and RSR decrements it; discusses MOP38/39 and INTR.

ein_diagram.title: Figure 4.19: EIN followed by RSR
ein_diagram.comment: Explicit delayed enable; RSR execute row is labeled F1, unlike the skipped-to-F2 presentation later.

interrupt_circuit.title: Figures 4.20/4.21
interrupt_circuit.comment: INTR→INTA clocked F0T0, then the entry table clears INTE/INTR, increments N and writes constant002 into the new PC. No PG change is shown. Adjacent reset table is distinct; not evidence RSR alone re-enables INTE.

jmp.title: Figure 5.3: JMP MOP table
jmp.comment: F1T1 MOP31 changes phase to F2 without restarting T; F2T5 reads target; F2T6 writes PC and PG. Prose also specifies JCR register target.

calls.title: Figure 5.4: JSR and RSR
calls.comment: JSR increments caller PC again during F1, increments N at F2T2 and writes target to new PC at F2T6. RSR skips phase then decrements N.

branch_circuit.title: Figure 5.5: conditional branch circuits
branch_circuit.comment: MOP51–54 select Z/L/T/DI bit0; MOP55 clocks H at T2. XOR uses IR bit3; inverted H output gates MOP22 at T6. Separate T capture edge and complete branch/page decoding are not drawn.

branch_sequence.title: Figure 5.6: BB0 functional/MOP sequence
branch_sequence.comment: Operand fetch increments PC; conditional MOP22 at F2T6 selects branch or fall-through.

and.title: Figure 5.7: AND microprogram
and.comment: R(A) and X operands, X→DI/DB→BR preparation, Z from ALU result. Numbered row sparse; held levels need reconstruction.

inc_dec.title: Figure 5.8: INR/DCR microprograms
inc_dec.comment: Increment and complemented increment/decrement; captures and final register writes. Held gates across phases are implicit; the three-cycle model uses both F1 and F2 without a phase skip.

shift.title: Figure 5.9 and omitted DCR flag circuitry
shift.comment: SHR/ROR/RRL semantics; explicitly says DCR zero-detection controls omitted from figure 5.8.

mux.title: Figure 5.10: shift multiplexer
mux.comment: MOP11 shifts ALU→BR. ROR wraps bit0; SHR grounds bit7; RRL uses a master/slave Link. Explicitly says figure-5.11 gates are only a principle and physical controls are partly coded.

rrl.title: Figures 5.11/5.12: RRL circuits and microprogram
rrl.comment: Link path and shift timing. Printed 30 at F1T1 conflicts with functional 2→F; figure 5.11 uses 57 for zero insertion.

io_out.title: Figure 6.11: output port
io_out.comment: Address decode + EDE + WRITE loads port latch. Prose prints output address 001; figures 6.10/6.11 show 00. Accepted project correction E007 changes the output address to 00; input address 001 remains correct.

io_in.title: Figures 6.12/6.13: input port
io_in.comment: EDE and physical DBDIR high admit read data; tristate otherwise.

control.title: Figure 6.14: SCW/SCS
control.comment: STRCS accompanies the second byte on DB; figure 6.14 illustrates an external latch as one possible receiving circuit, not required CMC8 hardware. Separate interface from LRD/SRD.

handshake.title: Figure 6.15: SCS vs SCW
handshake.comment: SCS continues after strobe; SCW waits for active-low SCWR acknowledgement.

scw_intro.title: SCW microprogram introduction
scw_intro.comment: Opcode fetch and second control-byte address; wired acknowledgement context.

scw_sequence.title: Figure 6.17: SCW microprogram
scw_sequence.comment: SCWR sampled at F2T4 and each wait T4. Figure6.17, figure6.18 and later prose put PME rise F1T2/strobe F1T6; one earlier paragraph says F2T2/F2T6. E008 selects the consistent F1 labels without altering literal source.

test_inputs.title: Figure 6.22: test inputs
test_inputs.comment: Four direct test lines and BT0/BT1; compares software subroutine, interrupt and test-input polling.

bidirectional.title: Figure 7.5: bidirectional port
bidirectional.comment: A register behaves like a memory word activated by EDE rather than PME/SME.

memory_test.title: MIDAHS memory and port tests
memory_test.comment: Parallel SRM/LRM and SRS/LRS programs; LRM data window F2T2–T5; LRD/SRD opcodes in lower table.

delay_loop.title: Figure 8.5: wait subroutine
delay_loop.comment: LRI, INR, BZ0, DCR, RSR with octal machine code and per-instruction cycles; INR explicitly three cycles.

delay_measure.title: Wait-subroutine timing
delay_measure.comment: JSR call example; computed timing uses (3+2) cycles for INR+branch. SCW used as halt in this system setup.

traffic1.title: Figure 8.6 part 1
traffic1.comment: LRM/SRD, BT1, JMP and repeated JSR calls with octal encodings. Complete 75-byte figure8.6 image is transcribed in traffic-program.json and exercised by the board harness. E010 retains the inconsistent T1/T2 prose comment beside actual T1/T3 instructions.

traffic2.title: Figure 8.6 part 2
traffic2.comment: NOP padding; LRI/INR/BZ0/DCR/RSR delay routine. Printed octal172 is retained; its parenthetical decimal76 conflicts with decimal122 and the p.144 calculation (candidate E009).

lamp_code.title: Figure 6.9: lamp polling example
lamp_code.comment: LRI/SRD/LRD/ANI/BZ0 polling sequence; generic OUT/STORE references in surrounding prose are not CMC8 mnemonics.

lamp_explanation.title: Lamp polling interpretation
lamp_explanation.comment: Explains immediate data load, port transfer and ANI mask replacing accumulator contents; octal numeric notation.

kex_start.title: Figure 8.8: KEX initialization
kex_start.comment: Text names LSX R5 after copying the address into X; system memory-selection wiring must be considered separately.

keyboard.title: Figure 8.10: keyboard subroutine
keyboard.comment: CPY R6→R7, XRI R7 with octal 377, zero branches and RSR. Several printed mnemonic/machine-code pairs disagree with figure 5.1. E004/E005 are accepted byte-field corrections: 052→057 at 012 and 340→343 at 014; preserve the printed fields.

key_sort.title: Figure 8.11: key identification
key_sort.comment: LRI R4, SHR R6 and BB0 R6 distinguish command bits; example octal encodings.

increment_key.title: Figure 8.12: increment-address command
increment_key.comment: LRD R7, INR R7, SRD R7, LRX R5, SRD R5, JMP page3; SRD R7 machine-code field prints 032 instead of expected 037. Accepted project correction E006: R7 is intended by the read/increment/write sequence.

jmp_bus.title: Figure 6.7: JMP bus timing
jmp_bus.comment: Target is written to PC at the beginning of F2T6; AB receives it at T1 of the following fetch. Confirms operand address remains in AB across the jump completion.

jmp_phase_context.title: JMP combined execute cycle discussion
jmp_phase_context.comment: Explains the F1–2 execute cycle used in the following JMP timing diagram.

jmp_single_step.title: Figure 6.8: single-step JMP
jmp_single_step.comment: Shows memory/address retention through single-step waits and the T4 WAIT-output mask. Implemented in v018 with explicit H023 SSE timing/interaction assumptions; the omitted complete SSE circuit is not claimed recovered.

test_inputs_context.title: CMC8 test-input discussion; then Intel 8048 comparison
test_inputs_context.comment: Opening paragraph loosely calls BT actions subroutine jumps. No N increment or return-address mechanism is specified; later 8048 discussion belongs to another architecture.

lamp_zero.title: Lamp polling: ANI result and Z
lamp_zero.comment: Opening paragraph explicitly says ANI gives Z=0 for a nonzero masked accumulator result, causing BZ0 to repeat; low input bit3 lets execution continue. No internal capture slot is given.

serial_link.title: CMC8 Link and serial transfer
serial_link.comment: CMC8 has direct LOUT from Link. Eight RRLs emit a register LSB first; setting Link from a test input before each RRL permits serial reception. Earlier UART/SCMP comparisons do not define CMC8 circuitry.

scw_timing.title: Figure 6.18: SCW handshake timing
scw_timing.comment: Strobe F1T6; PME/control-byte address/data held through two complete waits (16 extra subdivisions), then F2T6 releases PME. SCWR low around T4 ends waiting. Later PIO examples on this page are other-architecture context.

wait_phase.title: Memory-ready wait-cycle mechanism
wait_phase.comment: Eight-subdivision F3 waits suppress normal instruction MOPs. MEMR high means not ready; low resumes. Execute-phase reads can wait as well as fetch. v018 implements a selected continuation controller; SCWR uses the same loop mechanism with its own checkpoint.

kex_start_code.title: KEX startup listing
kex_start_code.comment: Initial JMP on page 3 targets 017, immediately after the keyboard routine listing; adjacency supports but alone does not prove that routine’s page.

kex_layout.title: Figure 8.9: KEX registers, memory and control words
kex_layout.comment: KEX start address is program-memory page 3, octal 363.

reset_prose.title: RESET: T7 sampling and following reset cycle
reset_prose.comment: MOP47 is active only during T7. A low RESET during T7 selects the following machine cycle: clear INTA/PG at T0, DI=0 at T1, N=0 at T2, DI→R0 at T4. Does not describe additional flag clears.

reset_sequence.title: Figure 4.21: RESET gate and functional cycle
reset_sequence.comment: Separate from interrupt figure 4.20 on the same page. Figure4.21b specifies F0 reset cycle with INTA/PG clear T0, zero DI T1, N clear T2, R(N) write T4 and phase reset T7. No numbered INTA-clear MOP is given.

wait_circuit.title: Figure 4.15: HALT and MEMR circuitry
wait_circuit.comment: HALT latch set during F0T2, cleared by high HALT. WAIT samples HALT.Q OR gated raw MEMR at T4; active-low WAIT output is forced high during T4.

memory_wait_timing.title: Figure 4.16: LRS with one wait per memory read
memory_wait_timing.comment: Three phases consume six machine cycles. Each wait runs from T4 through the following T3; PME/SME and AB remain stable, then original phase resumes at T4.

halt_wait_prose.title: HALT/MEMR timing explanation
halt_wait_prose.comment: MEMR sampled at beginning T4; WAIT pin asserted after T4. HALT high asynchronously clears its request latch; low must reach the F0T2 set window. Returning work resumes at F0T4.

halt_wait_timing.title: Figure 4.17: HALT during LRS
halt_wait_timing.comment: Three wait cycles delay the opcode fetch. WAIT output pulses high during each T4. HALT release resumes fetch before operand/data phases.

single_step_prose.title: Single-step SSE handshake
single_step_prose.comment: SS is consulted with HALT low. SS high sets SSE; SS low with SSE=1 clears SSE and permits one instruction. Held-low SS with SSE=0 does not permit another instruction.

single_step_flow.title: Figure 6.6: single-step state diagram
single_step_flow.comment: The HALT-low branch tests SS and SSE; completed instruction returns to next opcode address presentation before waiting. Complete SSE circuit omitted.

single_step_timing.title: Single-step JMP timing explanation
single_step_timing.comment: SS must be low during a later T3 to leave the ordinary wait. After one instruction, the next fetch waits while SSE=0. Full SSE circuit is not supplied.

traffic_lamps.title: Figure8.3: ED4 traffic lamp bit patterns
traffic_lamps.comment: Main road red/yellow/green bits0/1/2; side road red/yellow/green bits5/6/7. Codes044,046,041,201,301 octal. Green+yellow overlaps are part of the illustrative example.
